properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 11:21AM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by earlier excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...Southeastern York County in east central Nebraska...
Northwestern Fillmore County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1110 AM CDT, various rainfall observations, automated river
gauges, and ground-truth reports from observers indicated that at
least 2-4 inches of rain had fallen within the area over the last
24 hours, resulting in continued flooding along area creeks and
rivers. Specifically along the West Fork Big Blue River in
Fillmore and York counties, an automated gauge north of Grafton
reported a stage of 12.9 feet at 1100 AM CDT,  which was 1.9 feet
above minor flood stage of 11.0 feet. As a result, widespread
flooding of pastures and fields along the river continues, as
confirmed by an observer in the McCool Junction area. Going
forward, it is likely that water levels along the West Fork Big
Blue River will remain in minor flood stage until at least
sometime on Friday before slowly falling below flood stage, but
exact timing is a bit uncertain as upstream water continues to
feed into the river from smaller creeks.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Elk Run Creek, Stone Creek, Antelope Creek, West Fork Big Blue
River, School Creek and Galaway Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction, and rural areas along the West Fork Big Blue
River both upstream and downstream of McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
A second release from Suicide Basin has started and levels will
continue to drop into Friday. Levels on the Mendenhall are rising and
will continue through the release.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 745 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent or occurring. Water levels will,
continue to rise and water temperatures will fall within the lake,
and river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1017 AM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from a glacier-dammed lake outburst across the warned
area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly,
especially near The Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 9:45am the stage was 5.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest between 9.8 to 10.3 feet is expected around
2:00pm to 6:00pm Friday. Water levels will go above minor flood
stage around 10:00am Friday. Water levels will reach moderate
flood stage around 2:00pm to 6:00pm Friday.

Impacts:
At 6.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the "causeway"
at the end of the trail.
At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.
At 9.0 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.
At 9.5 feet: Water levels up to 0.5 feet will cover Skaters Cabin
Road between Skaters Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead. Campsite 7
will be flooded with water starting to flow over the road between
campsites 8 and 9 in the Mendenhall Campground.
At 10.0 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with
up to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.
